findings.description: Critical: `_complete_completion_ledger` passes `agent_id=os.environ.get("AGENT_ID")` into `complete_work`, but atomic `claim_immediately` submit always claims as `resolve_identity(principal, None, None)` (bound principal or unbound `cloud-agent`). When `AGENT_ID` is set under an unbound key, complete runs as the session id against a row claimed by `cloud-agent` and `complete_task` returns `task_not_found_or_not_claimed_by_agent`; bound keys with a mismatched `AGENT_ID` 403. Design D2 and the bridge handoff path already require omitting request identity so the server resolves ownership — this breaks ledger persistence and withholds terminal envelopes.
findings.resolution: Pass `agent_id=None` from `_complete_completion_ledger` (same pattern as `try_handoff_write` when an API key is present) so complete uses the authenticated principal that owned the atomic claim. Add an end-to-end test: claim_immediately submit then complete with `AGENT_ID` set under unbound and bound keys.

findings.description: Critical: `http_proxy.proxy_submit_work` does not forward `claim_immediately`, so the MCP/HTTP-proxy path cannot open an atomically claimed completion-ledger row. Design D2 and the dispatcher bridge path require atomic submit-and-claim before vendor launch; MCP consumers of `proxy_submit_work` are stuck on the race-prone submit-then-claim path the recovery removed.
findings.resolution: Add `claim_immediately: bool = False` to `proxy_submit_work` and include it in the POST `/work/submit` body. Mirror any MCP `submit_work` tool signature the same way. Cover with a proxy unit test asserting the flag is sent.

findings.description: Nit: `042_atomic_submit_claim.sql` creates `submit_claimed_task` without `REVOKE ALL ... FROM PUBLIC`, explicit `GRANT EXECUTE ... TO service_role`, `SECURITY INVOKER`, or pinned `search_path`, unlike sibling `042_atomic_routing_audit.sql`. PostgreSQL still grants EXECUTE to PUBLIC by default, so the privileged insert-as-claimed RPC is wider than the hardened sibling.
findings.resolution: Match the sibling migration: `SECURITY INVOKER`, `SET search_path = public, pg_temp`, `REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION submit_claimed_task(...) FROM PUBLIC`, and `GRANT EXECUTE ... TO service_role`. Extend `test_atomic_submit_claim_migration.py` to assert those clauses.

findings.description: Nit: This recovery adds a second migration numbered `042` (`042_atomic_submit_claim.sql`) beside adaptive-router’s `042_atomic_routing_audit.sql`. The runner applies both by filename, so boot is fine, but ops docs and “apply migration 042” language become ambiguous; the file should be `043_...` on this branch.
findings.resolution: Rename to `043_atomic_submit_claim.sql` (and update the migration unit-test path). Prefer unique numeric prefixes going forward even though filename+checksum tracking tolerates collisions.

findings.description: Nit: Migration comments and Python enforce that atomic claim is only for dependency-free, non-projection tasks without `agent_requirements`, but `submit_claimed_task` itself performs a bare INSERT into `claimed` with no SQL-side checks. Any direct RPC caller can bypass queue eligibility and create self-owned claimed rows.
findings.resolution: Reject non-null `depends_on` / projection / `agent_requirements` inside the SQL function (or refuse unexpected `input_data` keys), mirroring the Python `atomic_claim_incompatible_options` gate, so the database remains the authority.

findings.description: Nit: The vendor-result envelope schema allows terminal states (`succeeded`/`failed`/`cancelled`) with null or omitted `vendor_task_id`, and `parse_vendor_result_envelope` accepts that, but `poll_for_result` treats `envelope.vendor_task_id != task_id` as protocol corruption — so a schema-valid terminal envelope with `vendor_task_id: null` fails the ledger closed.
findings.resolution: Either require `vendor_task_id` on terminal poll responses in the schema/parser, or treat null terminal `vendor_task_id` as “unchecked” and only compare when present. Add a contract test covering both sides.

findings.description: Nit: Async submit logs only the vendor `task_id` (`Async task submitted for %s: task_id=%s`) and `write_manifest` omits `ledger_task_id`, `task_id`, and `async_dispatch` from durable dispatch records, so operators cannot correlate coordinator ledger rows with review artifacts despite NFR observability requiring one ledger work id per async lifecycle.
findings.resolution: Log both `ledger_task_id` and `vendor_task_id` on submit/poll/complete paths, and include `ledger_task_id` / `task_id` / `async_dispatch` in manifest dispatch entries.

findings.description: FYI: `GET /locks` and `POST /locks/release-by-agent` correctly bind identity for bound API keys, but under legacy unbound keys `resolve_identity` trusts the request `agent_id`, so a shared unbound key can list/bulk-release another agent’s locks. This matches pre-existing unbound acquire/release semantics and design’s cloud-agent fallback, but bulk release widens blast radius versus single-path release.
findings.resolution: Accept while unbound keys remain supported; prefer bound keys in production. If unbound keys stay long-term, consider restricting release-by-agent to the `cloud-agent` fallback identity only unless an explicit admin capability is present.

findings.description: Optional: A non-zero async status CLI exit immediately completes the ledger as failed and returns, while a poll subprocess timeout only retries. A flaky status command can therefore permanently fail a still-running vendor task.
findings.resolution: Accept fail-closed for now, or treat transient status exit codes like poll timeouts (retry until deadline) while still failing closed on definitive protocol/auth errors.

findings.description: none: Atomic `claim_immediately` + `submit_claimed_task` closes the submit-then-claim race; ledger open failure prevents vendor launch; malformed/timeout/mismatch paths complete the ledger failed; successful findings are withheld when `complete_work` fails; regex poll fields are removed; live async CLI lanes are unadvertised per D4; SDK alternative/quick reject before SDK calls; lock list/release-by-agent and deregister hook wiring match the lock-recovery requirement.
findings.resolution: Keep these patterns; fix finding #1 before relying on the async ledger in sessions where `AGENT_ID` is set.
